name: St. Louis Union Station
elevationDatum: Local rigid exterior footing plane y=0; real metres, +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Mapped rotation is baked once; no DEM, sea-level or Mercator scale.
note: The municipalpreservationrecord gives230ft for the eastclocktower; ASCEgives232ft, while restoration andotheraccounts give280ft. This model adopts the municipal230ft(70.104m) and records the unresolved discrepancy rather than claiming a survey. Current2025towerphoto2and MarketStreetfront3were checked;1and4are interior/train references, not exterior massing sources. The three headhousepavilions, hippedredroofs, pairedfrontturrets, tallclockshaft and small attached octagonal turret are retained. The exact unifiedOSMbuilding includes the long train-shed complex; its rear canopies are a deliberately simple open structural abstraction with grounded posts and closed thin roofs, not a giant solidbox. Currentaquariuminteriors, rides, detachedrestaurants, forecourts and figurativeornament are outside this sourceasset. Clock faces are procedural unnumbered disks; no words, signs, logos, flags orreferenceimagery. y0 is a single rigidexteriorfooting plane; no terrainbaked and bothappmodesuntested. Cityscape: not tested. Full 3D world: not tested. Review follow-up: Added tiled contrasting hands to all four 1.9 m-radius clock dials: 0.9 m hour hand, 1.4 m minute hand, both 0.16 m wide, with 12 ticks near and four far. The hands and ticks replace holes in the dial polygons on the same plane, so there are no overlapping dial faces or depth offsets. Both LODs keep readable unnumbered clocks.
